newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders say investment to secure jobs.
newsitem.headline: German builders say investment to secure jobs.

text.p: Leading employers in Germany's construction industry said on Friday that a planned investment of some 38 billion marks ($22.5 billion) in large infrastructure projects would over the next five years save some 76,000 jobs in the sector.

German Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann, present at industry discussions in Bonn, urged private sector organisations to become involved in the financing of public infrastructure projects, a move he said would boost investment further without overburdening state finances.

The talks, which included representatives from Germany's two main employer groups, trade union leaders and government officials, took place against a background of particularly severe unemployment in the German construction sector.

The German Federal Labour Office estimated earlier this month that winter unemployment in the country's construction-related industries accounted for nearly half of the 510,000 jump in overall joblessness in January.

German building unions and employers said the rise, which means that one in every three builders are unemployed, was partly a consequence of the scrapping of "poor weather" payments to staff by the government last winter.
The end of the poor weather payments has meant that many firms prefer to lay off workers in times of bad weather rather than keeping them on.

Referring to private finance schemes, Wissmann said there were currently 17 planned projects around the country, for a total investment of 6.8 billion marks, which offered opportunities for private sector operators.

Under the financing model envisaged by Wissmann, which is similar to Britain's private finance initiative, private companies would arrange the financing for an infrastructure such as a tunnel or a bridge and be paid back over time by charges made for usage by the public.
